organizations.What they build: One of France's largest robotics labs (CNRS). Teams Gepetto (humanoid motion generation), RIS (robotics & interactions) and RAP (robot action & perception). Gepetto co-develops the open-source Pinocchio (rigid-body dynamics) and Crocoddyl (optimal control) libraries that many legged-robot and humanoid labs use, and runs the Pyrène humanoid (PAL Robotics TALOS).
organizations.Warm contact path: Contribute to Pinocchio/Crocoddyl on GitHub, then contact Gepetto maintainers (unknown direct path)

organizations.What they build: Montpellier CNRS/University lab for computer science, robotics and microelectronics. Its robotics department works on humanoids, interaction and control; co-develops mc_rtc, an open-source real-time control framework for simulated and real robots (with CNRS-AIST JRL).

Inria/IRISA team on sensor-based and interactive robotics: visual servoing (controlling a robot from camera images), haptics, aerial and medical robots. Maintains ViSP, the open-source visual-servoing and tracking library.
Inria team (with CRIStAL / Univ. Lille) on soft and flexible robots made of deformable materials: modelling, simulation and control, built on the open-source SOFA simulation framework.
Inria / ENSTA team on developmental AI: curiosity-driven learning, autotelic agents and language-model agents, historically applied to robots (origin of the open-source Poppy robot platform).
Inria/LORIA team on life-long autonomy and interaction skills for robots in sensing environments (past projects ANDY, RESIBOTS on robots that adapt to damage with learning).

Inria Human-Centered Robotics team: humanoid and legged robots that work with people, learning and generative-AI methods for control of legged robots (partnership with UCL), open-source software and spin-offs.
Inria project team hosted at ENSC (Bordeaux INP) designing collaborative robots and robotic assistance for humans at work, mainly in industry (ergonomics, human-robot collaboration).
Inria team on cooperative and human-aware robot navigation in dynamic environments: multi-robot systems, human-centred robotics, perception and decision for autonomous agents.

Inria team developing intelligent, autonomous mobile robots that collaborate to achieve tasks in dynamic environments (perception, decision and control for multi-robot systems); runs public robotics seminars.

Autonomous-robotics research group of LaBRI (Univ. Bordeaux, ENSEIRB-MATMECA, CNRS). Builds small humanoids for RoboCup (SigmaBan) and agricultural robots; released Microban, a fully 3D-printable open-source humanoid (Raspberry Pi Zero 2W + 19 Dynamixel servos).

Nantes digital-sciences lab (CNRS, Centrale Nantes, Nantes Univ., IMT Atlantique) with a large robotics pole; e.g. team ROMAS on robotised 3D printing of large structures, platform TIRREX-XXL for large-space robotics.
Strasbourg engineering/computer-science/imaging lab; its Imaging-Robotics-Health activity builds surgical robots and medical-imaging systems.
CNRS/UTC lab (since 1981) on embedded systems that make mobile robots autonomous; runs an instrumented vehicle fleet for driver assistance and a mini-drones/mobile-robots platform.
Clermont-Ferrand CNRS/UCA lab with an image, perception systems and robotics axis; recent PhDs on manipulation of deformable objects and perception.
Grenoble signal/control lab; designs many custom flying robots (aerial robotics and embedded software) and works on robotics, intelligent vehicles and Industry 4.0.
~80-person department combining microrobotics, mechatronics, control and data science (robots and actuators at micro scale).
CNRS/Univ. Poitiers/ISAE-ENSMA physics and engineering lab; includes robotics and human-machine interaction work (e.g. a painting robot).

France 2030 priority research programme on 'organic robotics' (robots socially adapted to humans and their environment): 3 scientific challenges, 7 targeted projects, €34M budget, ~70 PhD students; the national robotics research umbrella.

CNRS national robotics research network: directory of ~49 robotics labs, working groups (humanoids, learning & neuroscience, manipulation, autonomous vehicles...), annual JNRR days, thesis prizes, education (AT1) and outreach; 3,249 registered members incl. 1,438 students.

robots_models.Name: Pinocchio
robots_models.Key specs: C++/Python rigid-body dynamics and kinematics (URDF), analytical derivatives, code generation
robots_models.Why it matters: Fast dynamics library behind many MPC/whole-body controllers; essential if we move from learned policies to model-based control.

robots_models.Name: Crocoddyl
robots_models.Key specs: Optimal control under contact sequences, DDP-based solvers
robots_models.Why it matters: Reference open-source optimal-control solver for legged/humanoid motion.

robots_models.Name: Pyrène (TALOS humanoid)
robots_models.Why it matters: France's flagship research humanoid, used for Gepetto's motion-generation work.

robots_models.Name: ViSP
robots_models.Key specs: Visual servoing, model-based/KLT/blob tracking, robot & sensor interfaces
robots_models.Why it matters: Ready-made camera-in-the-loop control for low-cost arms.

robots_models.Name: SOFA
robots_models.Key specs: Interactive soft/rigid body mechanics simulation; current release v26.06 (2026)
robots_models.Why it matters: Main simulator for soft robots; summer school 'Deformations in Robotics'.

robots_models.Name: mc_rtc
robots_models.Key specs: Real-time control framework for simulated and real robots (humanoids, HRP-4 demos)
robots_models.Why it matters: Production-grade QP whole-body control used on humanoids.

robots_models.Name: SigmaBan
robots_models.Why it matters: Proof that a university group can build competitive small humanoids.

robots_models.Name: Microban
robots_models.Key specs: Fully 3D-printable humanoid, Raspberry Pi Zero 2W, 19 Dynamixel servomotors
robots_models.Why it matters: Low-cost open humanoid we could replicate as a hardware onboarding project.

robots_models.Name: Poppy robots (Poppy Humanoid / Ergo Jr)
robots_models.Key specs: Open-source 3D-printed robot platform for education, arts and research
robots_models.Why it matters: French open-hardware robot lineage (also the origin of Pollen Robotics).

robots_models.Name: DUSt3R
robots_models.Price / access: Code and weights on GitHub (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, non-commercial)
robots_models.Key specs: Geometric 3D reconstruction from image pairs without camera calibration
robots_models.Why it matters: Cheap 3D perception from plain cameras for low-cost robots.

robots_models.Name: Solo (ODRI open quadruped)
robots_models.Builder (if not in map): Open Dynamic Robot Initiative (multi-lab; incl. Gepetto team, LAAS-CNRS)
robots_models.Key specs: Open torque-controlled modular architecture for legged locomotion research
robots_models.Why it matters: Open-source torque-controlled legged robot: a possible ambitious hardware target.

summary: Who leads: French academic robotics is dense and public: LAAS-CNRS (Pinocchio/Crocoddyl, humanoids), LIRMM (mc_rtc), Inria teams (Rainbow/ViSP, DEFROST/SOFA, Flowers, HuCeBot, Larsen, Chroma) and NAVER LABS Europe lead, networked by the CNRS GdR Robotique (49 labs, 3,249 members) and the France 2030 PEPR O2R programme.

Where money is: labs are funded by CNRS/Inria/ANR and France 2030 (PEPR O2R, TIRREX infrastructure), not by students; the only corporate research lab with real budget in this slice is NAVER LABS Europe, and IRT Jules Verne brings industrial money.

Where demand is: ~100 student teams a year build robots for the Coupe de France de Robotique / Eurobot (Planète Sciences); dozens of engineering-school clubs (Eirbot, ClubElek, Robotronik, RobotESEO, INTech, ECEBORG...) are strong in mechanics/electronics but almost none do robot learning, which is our gap to fill.

Gap/opportunity: academic open-source tools (Pinocchio, ViSP, SOFA, mc_rtc, Microban) are free building blocks; schools strong in mechanics (Arts et Métiers, Centrale Nantes, ENSEA for electronics) complement our software skills.

Best entry point: register as student members of GdR Robotique, enter (or co-train with a Paris club like VRAC/ARDIC, INTech, ECEBORG) for the Coupe de France de Robotique, and invite Rhoban/LAAS/Inria researchers as speakers on low-cost robot learning.
